title: ChatGPT as an AI L2 Teaching Support: A Case Study of an EFL Teacher
extended_summary:
This paper examines how an English as a Foreign Language (EFL) teacher used ChatGPT over seven months as a teaching support tool. The study asks how the teacher integrated ChatGPT into her practice, how effective it was for planning and teaching, how she prompted it to obtain useful outputs, and how she validated the reliability of the information it produced.

The intervention was not a formal experimental treatment but an exploratory single instrumental case study of one teacher in a private language school in Spain. The teacher used ChatGPT for lesson planning, in-class activities, and assessment-related tasks such as rubric creation, writing correction, feedback, and self-assessment activities. Data came from the teacher’s ChatGPT history, lesson plans, and a semi-structured post-interview, and was analyzed qualitatively with thematic analysis.

The paper concludes that ChatGPT can substantially support EFL teaching when teachers develop prompt-crafting skills and critically evaluate outputs. The teacher’s use of ChatGPT evolved over time from simple prompts to more structured multi-step prompts, which improved the usefulness of outputs. The authors argue that ChatGPT was most valuable for planning lessons, generating classroom materials, and supporting assessment, but that human judgment remained necessary because outputs could contain inaccuracies or bias. The study emphasizes critical AI literacy, prompt design, and verification practices as key competencies for effective use.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative single-case study with thematic analysis and interview data, so it provides rich descriptive evidence but no causal identification. It is peer-reviewed and empirically grounded, but credibility is limited by the single-participant design and lack of comparison group.
impact_tier_rationale: The study suggests practical benefits for teacher productivity and classroom use, but the evidence is not causal and no effect sizes are reported. Its impact is therefore promising but unclear/modest for broader K-12 populations.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used as an L2 teaching support tool for an EFL teacher to generate lesson plans, classroom activities, vocabulary materials, real-time Q&A, interactive language practice, and assessment prompts over a seven-month case study.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that ChatGPT was helpful for writing-related instruction and feedback, including lesson-plan generation for writing tasks, sentence/text editing, and assessment of student compositions. However, when benchmarked against Cambridge FCE writing scales, ChatGPT’s scores diverged from official examiner scoring by 3 points overall (e.g., Content 3 vs 4; Language 2 vs 3; Organisation 2 vs 3), indicating usefulness but imperfect accuracy.
finding.measure: Qualitative analysis of ChatGPT-generated writing tasks, lesson plans, and essay scoring compared with Cambridge FCE writing scales
finding.study_size: n=1 teacher case; specific essay example n=1

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT supported speaking and interactive language practice through role-play, simulated conversations, and real-time Q&A in class. The study is descriptive rather than causal, but the teacher reported increased student participation and enthusiasm during ChatGPT-supported activities.
finding.measure: Qualitative case study evidence from teacher prompts, lesson plans, and post-interview perceptions; classroom implementation examples
finding.study_size: n=1 teacher case with student groups across children, teenagers, and adults

finding.finding_summary: A recurring theme was development of prompt crafting, critical thinking, and students’ ability to evaluate AI outputs. The teacher explicitly framed ChatGPT use as a way to help students cross-check information, identify inaccuracies, and learn to use AI more autonomously and critically.
finding.measure: Thematic analysis of prompts, interview data, and reported reliability-checking strategies

finding.finding_summary: The teacher reported that ChatGPT saved time by helping with lesson planning, material creation, assessment rubrics, grading support, and feedback generation. The paper’s main practical conclusion is that ChatGPT considerably alleviated teacher workload, especially for low-complexity tasks and younger learners.
finding.measure: Teacher-reported workload reduction and qualitative analysis of planning/assessment tasks
